numerical_failure.observed_behavior: HDFStore.select with a "<" (or "<=") where-query on a datetime64/timedelta64 data column also returns the NaT rows, because NaT is stored as iNaT (int64 min) which sorts below every real value. Example: store.select("t", where="col < '2020-01-01 00:00:01'")["pos"].tolist() returns [0, 2].
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Only the row with a real value below the bound should match, i.e. [0]; NaT rows should not satisfy a "less than" query, consistent with the in-memory comparison.
trigger_conditions: HDFStore.select with a where-query using "<" or "<=" on a datetime64 or timedelta64 data column
column stored with NaT values (stored as iNaT, int64 min)

numerical_characteristics.dtype: int64 storage for datetime64/timedelta64 columns (NaT stored as iNaT)
numerical_characteristics.precision: The passages show datetime64 columns at unit 's' (as_unit('s')) and default ns; no explicit precision/tolerance number stated for float comparisons
category_specific_evidence: NaT in datetime64/timedelta64 columns is stored as int64 iNaT (int64 min), which sorts below every real value, so an unguarded '<' or '<=' where-query matches the NaT rows
Fix in BinOp.generate (pandas/core/computation/pytables.py) emits ((col != iNaT) & (col < val)) for '<'/'<=' when kind starts with datetime or timedelta; '>'/'>=' need no guard
PR#68031 reproducer: DataFrame with to_datetime([... , NaT]).as_unit('s') appended and selected with where "col < '2020-01-01 00:00:01'" returns [0, 2] instead of expected [0]
New tests test_select_ordering_comparison_skips_nat and test_select_ordering_comparison_skips_nat_on_index cover NaT on datetime/timedelta columns and index for '<', '<=', '>', '>='
test_append_with_timedelta previously asserted the old NaT-matching answers; expectations now computed from in-memory comparison df[df['C'] < ...]
reproduction_risks: NaT is not a float NaN; the special value is iNaT (int64 minimum) sentinel in integer storage, so reproduction must use datetime/timedelta NaT rather than np.nan
Behavior depends on column kind being datetime/timedelta; only data_columns=True columns hit the generated guard path
Reproducer relies on HDFStore append/select with where-string; index=False is used in the reproducer and index-path test
Signed zero, +/-inf and subnormals are not mentioned in any passage
